items.title: 10 Turn-Based RPGs With Virtually Perfect Combat Systems
items.summary: RPGs like Fire Emblem and Baldur's Gate have helped to refine turn-based combat to perfection.
items.content:
Gustave, Maelle, Lune, and Sciel exploring on the island in the early parts of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Image via Sandfall Interactive Add CBR on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Sage Negron Published Oct 24, 2026, 1:15 PM EDT Sage Negron is a freelance writer based in New York City. He has contributed to CBR in the past, as well as Looper and DualShockers. When he's not writing, he's usually playing video games or reading a good book. Sign in to your CBR account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Making a great combat system in a turn-based RPG is not easy. After all, there are so many games that feature this kind of system that each new one has to find a way to innovate in order for it to stand out.

Luckily, there are plenty of fantastic turn-based RPGs that put their own spin on the genre. And many of them also have strong stories and exceptional party members to match their great gameplay.

The protagonist's All Out Attack portrait, raising a hand to adjust his collar, from Persona 3 Reload. Image via Atlus Persona 3 Reload remade the PS2 classic from the ground up with many of the quality of life changes that made Persona 5 Royal such a smash. The turn-based combat also received some smart new additions to make battling more fun.

The player now has more control over party members, the Shift mechanic helps players take advantage of hitting enemy weaknesses, and the Theurgy moves add even more cinematic flair to finishing off battles. Persona 3 Reload ’s combat is easily the best in the series.

Baldur's Gate 3 Combat Image via Larian Studios Turn-based battles are just one of the many amazing aspects of Baldur’s Gate 3 . With just one roll of the d20 dice, a wide array of combat options are triggered that make each battle feel different from the last.

From there, it becomes an entirely new game, managing stats, using different magic attacks, and trying to get the advantage over enemies. Those experienced with tabletop RPGs will feel right at home with Baldur’s Gate 3 .

4 graded cards, 6 seconds each. Faster answers score more.

Must be 18+/19+ to participate depending on jurisdiction.

Clair Obscur Expedition 33 battle system Image via Sandfall Games Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 combined a lot of different systems to create engaging turn-based combat. Players have to juggle elemental affinities, action commands, and powerful special attacks each time they get into battle.

In addition, stat boosts from Pictos and Luminas can change how each battle goes. Parrying attacks can save a player’s life, and stunning an opponent at the right time is crucial.

The pyrokinetic ability Ignition in Divinity: Original Sin II. Image via Larian Studios Tactical strategy games offer some of the best turn-based combat around. Divinity: Original Sin II , from the makers of Baldur’s Gate 3 , offers a flexible combat system that adapts to whatever party that the player builds.

Players can take advantage of both the environment and the elements, break an opponent’s armor, and take the high ground to make the best use of the open-ended class system. Divinity: Original Sin II has a little bit of everything for everyone.

Octopath Traveler Screenshot of a character fighting enemes in turn based combat Image via Square Enix There are eight characters that the player can choose to follow the story of in Octopath Traveler . No matter what path the player takes, the turn-based combat remains just as fulfilling.

Combat revolves around the Break and Boost system. Destroying an opponent’s guard will Break them and leave them defenseless, and Boost points are used to inflict even more damage.

items.title: 10 Best Turn-Based RPGs of All Time, Ranked
items.summary: Turn-based RPGs like Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 put action RPGs to shame.
items.content:
clair obscur expedition 33 featured art Image via Sandfall Interactive Add CBR on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Sage Ashford Published Oct 23, 2026, 5:45 PM EDT Staff Writer for CBR, Sage Ashford has also written for Comicon as well as other sites such as The Gamer, and has been doing freelance work since 2014, and been working for CBR since 2016. His focus is primarily on spreading the word on obscure anime, comic books, and games whenever possible. Follow him on Twitter @ sageshinigami, or on YouTube @ nolevelcap. Sign in to your CBR account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread 2 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Even though action RPGs are often seen as more modern than their turn-based counterparts, turn-based RPGs have made a comeback in recent years. Last year's Game of the Year, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, has turn-based combat, and the turn-based Persona games have begun to eclipse the now-action RPG Final Fantasy titles in popularity.

The greatest turn-based RPGs find ways to make their combat feel dynamic, creating addictive battle systems and wrapping them all in an amazing story. Some turn-based RPGs tell classic fantasy stories, while others feel more modern and even futuristic, but they're all great examples of how good the genre can be.

Ochette, Castti, Throne, Osvald, Partitio, Agnea, Hikari, and Temenos at a camp in a forest in Octopath Traveler II Image via Square-Enix Square-Enix tapped into the charm of the 16-bit era with their Octopath Traveler series. Yet there's more to the franchise than being a nostalgic throwback. Octopath Traveler II tells eight stories of eight travelers who just happen to find themselves working together as they overcome major obstacles in their lives.

While the first game is more of a testing ground, the second title improves on every aspect to create a generational classic. The game's combat is exceptional thanks to a mix of the franchise's Boost system and every enemy having specific weaknesses that players have to discover on their own. It naturally encourages players to build a balanced party and commit to big moves to finish enemies off.

Rip Mystery Packs of Graded Cards & Collectibles

Image via Konami Suikoden V is one of the underrated classics of the PS2 era of gaming. Set in the Queendom of Falena, Suikoden V follows a prince trying to protect his family after his government is taken over in a coup. As ever with Suikoden games, the focus shifts away from the usual "save the world" plot and focuses on gathering a military capable of restoring peace to the land.

The Suikoden battle systems have always been fun thanks to the variety present. Suikoden V expands on the franchise's usual war battles, forcing players to learn how to wage war both on land and sea at the same time. Meanwhile, the duels remain just as intense as ever, while the six-on-six battles are unlike anything else on the market.

Sign in to claim your place on the leaderboard!

Super Mario RPG screenshot showing Mario, Mallow, Bowser, and Geon standing together while Mallow pointing at something Image via Nintendo Super Mario RPG: Legend of the Seven Stars is still just as fun today as it was when it was released. Despite a massive upgrade in graphics, it still retains the charm of the original and its cutesy, diorama settings for each stage. While the story isn't much to think about, the world-building given to the Mushroom Kingdom is awesome.

Though some people describe Super Mario RPG as an ideal RPG for newcomers , Square still managed to innovate with its combat. The timing-based attack and defense forced players to do more than just sit back and select options from a menu.

Players who mastered blocking at the right time could often avoid damage altogether, so there was plenty of incentive to get it right. The remake retains all of this and even adds some fun team attacks to shake things up.

Dragon Quest XI battle screenshot showing Erik blocking a high kick from Jade in the martial arts tournament Image via Square-Enix Dragon Quest XI is still the peak of traditional JRPG gaming, years later. It tells what feels like a traditional story early on, but adds enough twists and subversions for players to never really know where it's all going. Though it's one of the longer games out, it's also a delight to play, thanks to the variety in settings and the adorable Toriyama character designs.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has sold 8.7 million copies and made $366 million, analyst says, and that's despite the "Game Pass cannibalization"
items.summary: The majority of them are on PC
items.content:

(Image credit: Sandfall Interactive/Kepler Interactive) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has sold 8.7 million copies and generated $336 million in revenue since its launch last year, with the majority of sales on Steam despite being on PC Game Pass.

A post by Alinea Analytics breaks down how the last few Game of the Year award winners – Elden Ring, Baldur's Gate 3, Astro Bot, and Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 – have sold across their various platforms.

As one of the biggest games ever made, Elden Ring naturally leads with $2 billion from 36.4 million copies sold, and Baldur's Gate 3 isn't too far behind with $1.2 billion from 23.2 million copies sold. Meanwhile Astro Bot made $291 million across 4.7 million copies sold, which is natural being an exclusive and being a sadly niche genre (bring back platformers being the top genre I beg you).

Then comes the most recent and most-awarded Game of the Year winner , Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, which matched the record set by Baldur's Gate 3 by winning all five major GOTY awards . While not quite near the Elden Ring or Baldur's Gate 3 numbers, the indie title has made $366 million through 8.7 million copies sold.

However, unlike the other three games, Clair Obscur was also available for 'free' to Xbox Game Pass subscribers until last week, and during that time it brought in 4.3 million players across Xbox consoles and PC Game Pass users. This naturally had an impact on Xbox sales through what Alinea calls "Game Pass cannibalization", with only 5.5% of sales coming from Xbox users, but this didn't really seem to affect PC sales too much, as 58.8% of sales came from Steam users.

Gears of War E-Day sold just 62k copies on Xbox versus 1.7 million Game Pass players, analyst says Baldur's Gate 3 has sold over 23m copies, but only 1% of players have crossed 500 hour in playtime Ex PlayStation boss told Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 devs not to call it a turn-based RPG Despite this "cannibalization," Clair Obscur creative director Guillaume Broche has been positive about Xbox Game Pass , and its impact on the game. He notes that the subscription "lowered that barrier of entry," especially when turn-based RPG's could "put people who prefer more real-time action games off."

Meanwhile, Circana analyst Mat Piscatella says the game is "a great example of a game where its sales potential was likely increased because of its inclusion in a subscription service."

As more people got to try the game with the subscription fee as the only barrier to entry, word of mouth will surely grow. So sure, 4.3 million people experienced the game without buying it, but that doesn't mean that 4.3 million people would buy the game outright otherwise.

Pokemon with Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's combat sounds like a bonkers idea, but one fan's now given us a taste test.

items.title: Rayman Legends Retold Adds Baguette Outfits As Tribute To Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
It's Official, Rayman Legends Retold Is Getting Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Skins
items.summary: The skins that were claimed to be in Retold since before it was revealed have been officially confirmed.
items.content:
It's Official, Rayman Legends Retold Is Getting Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Skins From TheGamer (Written by George Foster) on October 21, 2026 | OpenCritic

Ubisoft has officially confirmed that Rayman Legends Retold will feature skins based on Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 ’s iconic baguette outfits.

As is almost the norm for Ubisoft games, Rayman Legends Retold was leaked well ahead of its announcement during a State of Play . One of the most interesting parts of the early reports was that Retold would feature some new crossover skins based on some surprising games outside of Ubisoft’s wheelhouse .

The leak claimed that Astro Bot and Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 were going to be represented through new outfits. It’s been so long since Retold was announced that it seemed like that rumour was nothing but hot air, but it was actually at least half true this whole time, as the Clair Obscur costumes have just been unveiled.

Ahead of Rayman Legends Retold’s appearance at Paris Games Week , Ubisoft fittingly confirmed that the game will feature a lovely nod to Clair Obscur Expedition 33. That nod is the inclusion of Clair’s beloved baguette outfits, which were thought up as a “tribute from one French studio to another”.

Loic Gounon talks to us about Retold’s recent delay, the possibility of revisiting other games, and much more.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 on PS5 Drops to New All-Time Low Price at Amazon With a Coupon
items.summary: Amazon has knocked Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 on PS5 down to a new all-time low price, but it's only available through a coupon. After clipping it on the store page, you can buy it for $34.65 rather than $49.99.
items.content:
If 2025's Game of the Year , Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, has been on your gaming wishlist, there's no need to wait for Black Friday sales to grab it at a discount. Amazon currently has its physical PlayStation 5 copy marked down to a new all-time low price of $34.65 - 31% off its list price - which you can get by ticking the coupon box on the store page ( see it here ).

This is the only way you'll be able to see this deal price at checkout, so don't forget to check the box before adding it to your cart. The coupon is also only available for a few more days, until October 26, so the clock is ticking to pick it up at this record-low price . Additionally, it's only available for PS5 users. If you're hoping to grab it for Xbox, you'll unfortunately have to pay full price.

If you are able to take advantage of it, though, this is quite an exciting deal to have pop up before Black Friday sales kick off. It beats where we saw it during Prime Day earlier this year and in the middle of summer when it had another coupon appear at Amazon .

And yes, there's every chance it will appear in Black Friday sales as well, but why wait to find out? Being able to grab this phenomenal game for $35 right now instead is well worth it.

Full of wonderful characters, an incredible story, and beautiful music, Clair Obscur is a game you certainly won't regret adding to your library. Our 9/10 review from Michael Higham said that it, "paints itself into the pantheon of great RPGs with a brilliant combat system and a gripping, harrowing story." So if this is your first time stepping into its world, you're in for an unforgettable time.

Of course, Black Friday sales are coming up fast, so there's sure to be even more gaming deals like this one popping up soon. But if you're hoping to check out some more early deals in the meantime, Amazon's dropped a new sale on select Square Enix games that's worth having a look at as well.

Hannah Hoolihan is a freelancer who writes with the commerce team here at IGN.

items.title: Rayman Legends Retold's New Baguette Costumes Are A Tip Of The Beret To Expedition 33
Expedition 33's Fan-favorite Costumes Are Unofficially Invading a Different Game
items.summary: Every game needs a baguette outfit
items.content:
Listen Thread Link copied to clipboard By Austin Manchester Published Oct 21, 2026, 12:01 PM EDT Austin Manchester is a writer and editor living in New York City. At Polygon, he covers gaming and entertainment news, reviews new video games, interviews behind-the-scenes talent, and more. He enjoys discovering hidden gems and sharing them with Polygon's audience. Previously, he was the gaming editor for AIPT Comics and has written for other outlets like XDA, How-To Geek, and The List. He enjoys soulslikes, character-driven RPGs, and third-person shooters plucked straight out of the Xbox 360 era. He also likes to flex his non-video game nerdy knowledge sometimes, whether that's explaining who's who in the new Wolverine game or recommending a comic book series about a sentient sword. News Every game needs a baguette outfit

Image: Sandfall Interactive/Kepler Interactive Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover Rayman Legends Retold Sign in to your Polygon.com account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Sandfall Interactive's award-winning Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 took the gaming world by storm last year as players enjoyed the role-playing game's serious themes and its goofy bits , like the "baguette" outfits. Equip those, and the downtrodden expeditioners will suddenly look as silly as can be with red berets, black-and-white-striped shirts, and baguettes tied to their backs.

In just a few weeks, those beloved baguette outfits will unofficially make their way into a new game from a different French studio as a way of paying homage to Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 .

Close Image: Ubisoft Image: Ubisoft Image: Ubisoft window.arrayOfGalleries["article-gallery-1-128518621"] = '" Close Image: Ubisoft Image: Ubisoft Image: Ubisoft "'; In December's Rayman Legends Retold , Rayman and Barbara will get their own baguette outfits. While the news release doesn't explicitly state they're inspired by Expedition 33 , it does say the outfits "offer a playful nod to a fellow game created in Montpellier." So, you know. Expedition 33 . "Subtly, [the outfits] honor a title that holds a special place in the hearts of the development team," the news release states, making me think Ubisoft and I have different definitions of the word "subtly."

The original Rayman Legends came out in 2013, so it's not quite as old as o ther games that are getting remakes this year. Ubisoft decided to remake Rayman's most recent game as a way to introduce the franchise to a new audience because "it's the richest version of the world, the widest set of characters," brand manager Loïc Gounon told Polygon .

From what we've played so far, Ubisoft is succeeding. " Rayman Legends Retold is an imaginative platformer offering vibrant worlds, engaging platforming sequences, and endearing personality that oozes from every beautiful crack in its wacky world," Polygon's Jason Venter wrote in his preview of the upcoming game .

Rayman Legends Retold will be released on Dec. 3 for Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, and Xbox Series X. The baguette outfits will be available at launch, and you won't have to unlock or purchase them.

items.title: GTA 6 squeaks into eligibility for The Game Awards 2026 by the smallest of margins - but can it break Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's record number of wins?
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 releases 19th November and The Game Awards cut-off is 20th November. It's a close call. But will GTA 6 win?
items.content:
Image credit: Rockstar News by Robert Purchese Associate Editor Published on Oct. 15, 2026, 4:10 p.m. 52 comments Follow Grand Theft Auto VI Prioritise us on Google This generation's mega-game, Grand Theft Auto 6 , will be eligible for The Game Awards 2026 by a matter of one day.

As highlighted on X by industry watcher Shinobi602 , the cut-off date for this year's The Game Awards is 20th November, meaning GTA 6 - which arrives on 19th November - can be nominated across the show's various categories in 2026 and can potentially win. "Games must be made commercially available to customers on or before Friday, November 20, 2026, at 9pm PT," The Game Awards' website FAQ states.

The fit is so snug it might appear an exception has been made for Rockstar's game, but as Shinobi602 also noted , cut-off dates have been pretty similar each year, varying only by a day or two.

With GTA 6 in contention, the question becomes one of how much it could dominate proceedings. Rewind to Rockstar's last big release - Red Dead Redemption 2 in 2018 - and that game took home four awards : Best Narrative, Best Audio Design, Best Score/Music, and Best Performance (won by Roger Clark for his portrayal of protagonist Arthur Morgan).

The current TGA record holder - the game to beat - is Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , which last year took home nine wins , including the coveted Game of the Year award. Before Clair Obscur, the previous leader was Baldur's Gate 3 , with six wins. GTA 6 is an order of magnitude larger in terms of budget, scope, and public anticipation than either game, especially Clair Obscur. The weight of expectation is on Rockstar, that's for sure.

The Game Awards 2026 takes place on 10th December, and usually bookends the year's industry activity, after which we all frantically try to decide what our personal games of the year are. Eurogamer, for full disclosure, is a member of The Game Awards jury, along with many other gaming websites.

Meanwhile, Rockstar released a new launch trailer for GTA 6 this afternoon, highlighting Jason and Lucia's steamy relationship - literally, as they frolic in the shower - and the strain of being in a high-stakes crime environment such as theirs.

Rockstar is also currently embroiled in an employment tribunal in Scotland revolving around the sudden firing of 31 staff from Rockstar North last year. Those affected call it union-busting, whereas Rockstar insists employees were fired for gross misconduct. The verdict is now not expected until well into November , almost bang on when GTA 6 releases.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Comes To Astral Ascent In New Crossover Update
items.content:
We've been patiently hoping that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 would make its way to Switch 2 ever since it consumed our every waking hour last year. Sandfall is still yet to make that happen, but in the meantime, we have a crossover with the wonderful roguelike Astral Ascent , which we can play right now.

As revealed in today's Triple-i Initiative showcase, the sublime platforming roguelike has been treated to a bunch of crossover content from the land of Lumière. This includes three brand new bosses (Golgra, the Mime and Pétank), new rooms inspired by the game, and recruitable Expedition ally summons, each of which comes with its own special skills.

Truthfully, it looks wonderful. The crossover brings Expedition 33's world into Astral Ascent's glorious pixel art, and the trailer alone was enough to bring a tear to this writer's eye.

Here's the full rundown of everything included in the update, as detailed on the Astral Ascent Steam page:

Three Exclusive Bosses Golgra, the Mime, and Pétank have invaded the Prison, each with brand-new combat mechanics built just for this crossover. - Golgra - Calm at first, but her kicks and gestral allies get brutal once her second phase kicks in. - The Mime - Hammers, nails, walls take them both down together, or they'll revive each other. - Pétank - Runs, then rains projectiles, clones, and explosions on you.

Three New Rooms Straight from the world of Expedition 33 : Lumière , the Gestral Village , and the Campfire . One appears at random before the final boss each run: pick Expedition 33 content or the Andromeda Bar, but choose fast, it won't come back this run!

Around the Campfire Recruit a member of the Expedition as a special summon, each with their own unique mechanic: - Gustave - Heals, boosts your attack, strikes with you, and charges up a devastating finisher. - Maelle - Shifts stance with your HP; hold one long enough for a powerful payoff attack. - Sciel - Draws cards : Moon for mana, Sun for direct strikes, Twilight for a big hit. - Lune - Casts elemental spells matching your build, building to a powerful finisher. - Verso - Rank rises on hit, drops on damage taken, push it high for a massive attack bonus. - Monoco - Draws a random card, each triggering a different monster summon. You'll only get one Expedition ally per run, so take your pick, and don't forget to give Esquie a hug!

All of this is available for free to everyone who has beaten Astral Ascent on Destiny Level 0. What an excuse to dive back in, eh?

Review Astral Ascent (Switch) - Probably The Best Roguelite Since Hades

items.title: Game Pass Is About To Lose Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 And Some Other Incredible Games
items.summary: The RPG sensation and more gems are leaving in October
items.content:
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was one of 2025’s best games and one of the best third-party releases ever to join Game Pass day-and-date. Players have now had over a year to finish the turn-based RPG, but for any subscribers who haven’t yet taken the plunge, time is running out. The GOTY winner is leaving Game Pass on October 15.

That leaves you just under two weeks to go and complete the journey or start it from scratch. You can rush the main story to clear it in under 30 hours, but if you want to mine all of the expanded content, a completionist run will take you more than twice that. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is one of the rare JRPG-inspired games that’s managed to break through in the modern era to a broader audience, in part thanks to its novel dodge and parry mechanics which inject some fresh energy into the usual turn-based grind. It’s also worth making it all the way through to hit the twist ending .

But Clair Obscur is also not the only great game leaving Game Pass this month . The full list includes:

Pacific Drive and A Plague Tale Requiem are both excellent, especially for the spooky month. The former is a sci-fi survival crafting game about navigating a zone full of strange anomalies with a haunted station wagon. The latter is about surviving a late medieval Europe infested with disease carrying rats. Donut County , on the other hand, is a light hearted puzzle game you can finish in just a few hours that is still one of my favorite indie games of all time.

items.summary: It seems like Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 really made an impact on Macron.
items.content:
It seems like Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 really made an impact on Macron.

(Image credit: Getty Images - Photo by Henrique Campos / Hans Lucas / AFP via Getty Images) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 21 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter One of the biggest videogames of 2025 was Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , a French JRPG that sold millions of copies, won armloads of awards, and earned not just one but two separate shout-outs from French President Emmanuel Macron. It must've made an even bigger impression on him than it first appeared, as over the weekend Macron announced a new "international videogame festival" that will take place in France.

Macron made the announcement during an address at the Lumiere Summit (via GamesRadar ), a conference where governments, businesses, creators, and "cultural institutions" can collaborate on the future of "cinema and the moving image." I assume that last bit is a just-missed translation of "motion picture," because that's clearly what the conference is about, but regardless, Macron used the moment to reveal his ambitions for a related-but-different effort.

"I firmly believe that videogames are part of our culture," Macron said (Google translated), adding that games should be considered part of France's cultural heritage, just as movies and "other creative endeavors" already are.

"Therefore, we will create an international videogame festival conceived from the outset as a major global event for creativity, innovation, gamers, and the industry. The great global successes of French videogames remind us of the richness of this creative endeavor, this creativity, which is also an industry. We must further celebrate it and strive to gain everyone's support."

Parce que les jeux vidéo font partie de notre culture, nous allons créer un festival international du jeu vidéo. pic.twitter.com/45g7UYfOzk September 7, 2026

Macron didn't mention Clair Obscur by name, but that has to be at the top of his mind. There's really no bigger outwardly French videogame of the moment, and as I said, he's called it out publicly at least twice in the past.

This Control-inspired action game set in a 'planet-scale alien mind' has one of the most stunning art styles I've seen this year Former PlayStation boss Shuhei Yoshida told Clair Obscur devs to not call it a 'turn-based RPG' so people wouldn't 'overlook' it Clair Obscur developers see Sony's no-disk announcement as 'a sad decision', because they 'like to go outside, buy a game, and come back home with it' But there are an awful lot of other really good made-in-France videogames out there. Ubisoft , headquartered in Saint-Mandé, France, makes quite a few of them, and there's also the Plague Tale series, Rematch , Jusant , Chants of Sennaar , Sifu , Stray , and casting a little further back, the biggest and best of them all (and this is not up for discussion), Another World.

Watch On Details of Macron's proposed new showcase weren't shared, but he did offer some insight into what he called " profound upheavals " in film, television, animation, and videogames, including artificial intelligence and the advent of platforms—I imagine a reference to things like Roblox, Netflix, and Paramount if it ever manages to complete the Warner acquisition—that "are transforming our habits."

From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews

"Faced with challenges that know no borders, no nation can act alone. That is why, in Saint-Paul-de-Vence, France and South Korea—two great nations of creation committed to cultural diversity and their sovereignty—are bringing together those who create, produce, finance, distribute, innovate, and decide. Our ambition: to forge new alliances between creators and technologies, public and private actors, cinema, television, platforms, and video games. So that this revolution opens up new possibilities without homogenizing our imaginations."

France already has one big videogame festival, Paris Games Week, but it's possible Macron is envisioning something more in the way of a cultural exchange program rather than a business-oriented event. We'll have to wait and see for that, just as we're now waiting to see what Clair Obscur developer Sandfall Interactive gets up to next .

items.content:
Expeditioners!

Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text!

This brings the total number of supported languages to 20!

With the new Arabic language support, we had to consider additional changes to the game’s UI to ensure a smooth and enjoyable experience for Arabic-speaking players around the world.

Adding Arabic localization has been a true team effort over many months, from the incredible adaptation and localization work carried out by the linguists, to reworking the vast majority of the user interface for right-to-left reading, all the way through localization testing.

Every team involved brought passion and dedication to making this possible, and we couldn’t be more grateful for their work. We hope this update makes the story feel even more personal to our players.

Today’s update also includes some additional fixes and improvements. Read the full patch notes here!

Thank you all so much for your continued support! <3

Tomorrow comes.

~ The Expedition 33 Team

Content

  • Fixed an issue where applying burn after an enemy has been stunned causes them to be able to act immediately after recovering from the stun.

    [/*]

    [/*]

    [/*]

    [/*]

    [/*]

    [/*]

    [/*]

    [/*]

We are aware of a crash affecting some of you when loading into the Reacher or going out of the Manor. This crash is related to some specific PC configurations. Until we fix this issue, you can work around it by setting ‘Global Illumination’ to anything below ‘Epic’ temporarily.

items.title: 1st Anniversary of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
items.summary: Expeditioners!! Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special
items.content:
Expeditioners!! 

 

Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. 

 

To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special piece of artwork that we hope you will enjoy! 

8 Million Copies Sold

We're so thrilled, and honestly still quite overwhelmed, to announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has officially reached 8 million copies sold!

Thank you so so much to every single person who has played, created art, shared, streamed, discussed, and supported this game!!

Game Update: New Haircuts + Patch Notes

We've pushed a fun little update live today: new haircuts are now available in-game, giving the expedition even more style to strut around in! 💅 

For the full list of changes, fixes, and improvements, you can read the patch notes here

Community Emotes

Our community is packed with phenomenally talented artists and we wanted to celebrate that today.  

We commissioned some of our amazing community creators to design official Expedition 33 emotes for you to use in your own channels! 

A massive thank you to IrunoArt, comickergirl (Sarah Leuver), and Bugyakis for their brilliant work on each of these!!

They're FREE to download and use here

Official Baguette Merch

In the mood to add some baguette to your wardrobe? 

We’ve partnered with Orcival and Le Béret Français to bring you the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 striped shirt and beret for your cosplays! 🥖    You can purchase the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Orcival mariniere here

And the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Le Béret Français beret is available to buy here

On top of that, keep an eye out for a limited number of units of the Monolith Set to be back in stock from our partners at Laced and Pix n' Love soon!! 

And Finally… Cake

It's been a big day for us. Thank you for making it possible. 🎂 

And if you know someone who wants to pick up the game, we're running a 20% sale right now on Steam - As well as some fun merchandise goodies available on our merch page!

Merch Page

From the bottom of our hearts, we’re so thankful to each and every one of you – this has been the best year of our lives, thanks to you. 

 

- The Expedition 33 Team

items.content:
Expeditioners!

Thank you for all of your reports - the details for the fixes in this patch are written out below:

Update On Sirene Crash

  • After a thorough internal investigation, the crash that occurred after defeating Sirene can no longer be reproduced on our end. If you keep getting this issue, we’d suggest updating your Windows to the latest version. If the issue persists, please submit a report and we’ll continue investigating.

    [/*]

Bug Fixes & Improvements

Photo Mode

  • Fixed facial hair of characters being blurred in the Photo Mode on the close distance if Shading was set to Epic.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue in Photo mode that prevented the Inner Cone Angle and Outer Cone Angle options from affecting the shape of the preview light source.

    [/*]

  • Photo Mode's spotlight and point light display has been modified to improve their visibility

    [/*]

Gameplay

  • Fixed an issue where loading a save while picking up a journal could cause that journal to disappear permanently and become impossible to collect again.

    • Missing journals are now also restored retroactively when loading affected saves.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Fixed a soft lock that could occur, during the Chromatic Glissando encounter in Sirene’s Dress level, when a dead expeditioner equipped with Shortcut and Second Chance pictos was swallowed.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on Gestral Beach where using the Rematch option after losing the volleyball minigame could create a blocked save.

    [/*]

  • Fixed a visual issue where characters affected by Inverted would not have the correct colour effect applied to their eyes.

    [/*]

Environment

  • Fixed various environment issues (collisions, misplaced assets, missing or incorrect footsteps SFX) across Verso's Drafts, the World Map, and other levels.

    [/*]

  • Fixed various lighting issues on Steam Deck in Verso’s Drafts, Endless Tower and Stone Wave Cliffs levels.

    [/*]

As always, thanks for your support and for your reports via the official Typeform - We'll continue monitoring the reports coming in and working on future fixes!

~ The Expedition 33 Team
